title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LENA'S CAR LOT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lena, a used car saleswoman from Wichita, Kansas.
Forty-four years old. Very good at her job.
And one Tuesday, her boss asked her to tell one small lie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FLOOD CAR
segments.quote: If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: A blue sedan had been sitting in a flood. Her boss said, just call it clean.
A young couple with a baby wanted that car.
Lena remembered a note on her dad's dashboard, from the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
So she told the couple the truth. They walked away. So did her job.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FORK
segments.quote: When you come to a fork in the road, take it.
segments.author: Yogi Berra
lines: That night, Lena sat in her car, eating a sad gas station hot dog.
Find another dealer? Or open her own lot?
Her uncle called, quoting the baseball legend Yogi Berra:
When you come to a fork in the road, take it.
Lena laughed. Then she took the road nobody expected: her own lot.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE GRAVEL LOT
segments.quote: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: She rented a gravel lot with three old cars and a folding chair.
In the tiny office, she taped up a line from the Greek thinker Epictetus:
First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
So she said it out loud. I'm the honest car lady.
Then she put a card on every windshield, listing every dent, leak and squeak.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE LEMON
segments.quote: Integrity without knowledge is weak and useless, and knowledge without integrity is dangerous and dreadful.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: Then she bought a pickup at auction. It died before she got it home.
Her mechanic friend Walt quoted the English writer Samuel Johnson:
Integrity without knowledge is weak and useless, and knowledge without integrity is dangerous and dreadful.
Translation: you're honest, Lena, but you can't tell a good engine from a toaster.
So Walt taught her, every Saturday, for a year.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE KEYS
segments.quote: Few things help an individual more than to place responsibility upon him, and to let him know that you trust him.
segments.author: Booker T. Washington
lines: Then a young dad walked in. The one from the flood car.
He'd lost his job and needed work. Lena remembered Booker T. Washington:
Few things help an individual more than to place responsibility upon him, and to let him know that you trust him.
She handed him the keys to the lot. That weekend, he sold four cars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE NEW SIGN
segments.quote: Honesty is the first chapter in the book of wisdom.
segments.author: Thomas Jefferson
lines: Today, Lena's lot has forty cars and a waiting list.
Over the gate hangs a new sign, with words from Thomas Jefferson:
Honesty is the first chapter in the book of wisdom.
And her old boss? He bought his last car from her. She told him about every scratch.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do right. Make the choice. Name who you are. Learn your trade. Trust people. Stay honest.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do what's right. Make the choice. Decide who you are. Learn your trade. Trust people. And stay honest.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And always check under the hood.
